doc.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024

title: Time machine: events he wishes he had heard
summary: He would like to have heard Parker, the Mulligan-Baker group at The Haig, Bix and Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Do you have a place that you wish you could have been, to get in a time machine and experience a particular recording, a particular event?

Yeah, I mean I guess we all have that. I don’t know if I could pinpoint one in particular but obviously Charlie Parker either you know the “Koko” session maybe or you know maybe a specific event but something. You know that was a name that I grew up with in Kansas City that helped me get into things because there was somebody that I knew was important, just like Count Basie, even when I didn’t know where they fit within things I knew they were important. So Charlie Parker, not for that reason but just for musical reasons I would love to be in that company of one of the historic events. I think as far as © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

the West Coast things are concerned I would have loved to have been able to hear that group with Gerry and Chet at The Haig for example. I’m sure I could think of dozens more but you know off the top of my head those type things, you know, hearing Dizzy and Bird together in their prime I think would have been for me — now of course I’d love to have heard Bix Beiderbecke, I would love to have heard Louis Armstrong and the Hot 5 session. I would love to have been able to actually witness some of those landmark big bang type of an event but you know all we can do is we listen to them thousands of times throughout our lifetime and we get as close as we can that way I suppose.
Yes. And on occasion we get to be in front of our musical heroes, which I did once with Cannonball Adderley, who is still my guy. Addendum, separate insert follows:
